description: A 58-year-old man presents with a reducible right groin swelling that appears on straining and reduces on lying. Examination confirms a direct inguinal hernia above the inguinal ligament medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is planned.

steps.description: Skin crease incision 2 cm above and parallel to the medial two-thirds of the inguinal ligament. Divide Scarpa's fascia. Achieve haemostasis with diathermy.
Divide external oblique aponeurosis along its fibres from the external ring. Identify and preserve the ilioinguinal nerve.
Mobilise the spermatic cord at the pubic tubercle. Encircle with a soft Penrose drain. Identify inferior epigastric vessels medially — direct hernia lies medial, indirect lies lateral.

For direct hernia: invaginate the sac with a continuous purse-string suture into the preperitoneal space. For indirect: dissect sac off cord structures to the neck at deep ring. Divide and ligate if small, or reduce if large.
Inspect the posterior inguinal wall (transversalis fascia). Confirm the direct defect in Hesselbach's triangle. Check femoral ring for concurrent femoral hernia.

Place a 7x15cm polypropylene mesh extending 2 cm medial to pubic tubercle. Suture medial end to pubic tubercle periosteum with non-absorbable suture. Suture inferior edge to inguinal ligament with running suture to the deep ring.

Tack superior edge of mesh to conjoint tendon/internal oblique with interrupted sutures. Create a tailored slit in the mesh for the spermatic cord; overlap the two tails at the deep ring and fix with sutures.
Close external oblique aponeurosis over the cord with a continuous absorbable suture, recreating the external ring. Ensure ilioinguinal nerve is not trapped.
Close Scarpa's fascia with interrupted absorbable sutures. Subcuticular skin closure with absorbable monofilament. Apply Steri-strips and dressing.

learningObjectives: Identify the boundaries of Hesselbach's triangle (direct hernia)
Distinguish direct vs indirect inguinal hernia using inferior epigastric vessels
Understand the layers of the inguinal canal
Perform tension-free Lichtenstein repair with correct mesh fixation
Identify and preserve the ilioinguinal nerve
